scenarioLedger.title: Cellulitis, Abscess, and Necrotizing Fasciitis
facts: Separate nonpurulent cellulitis, drained abscess and surgical necrotizing infection; MRSA coverage is risk selected. Do not routinely give antibiotics to uninfected dermatitis.

Diabetic foot: no antibiotic for an uninfected ulcer. Soft-tissue infection usually 1-2 weeks; individual extension for extensive/slowly resolving disease. Positive bone margin after minor amputation: up to 3 weeks; unresected osteomyelitis: 6 weeks. Select drugs by severity, cultures and source control.

Serious invasive MRSA treated with IV vancomycin: AUC24 target 400-600 mg*h/L assuming MIC 1 mg/L, achieved in 24-48 hours with validated monitoring. This is not an oral CDI or routine mild-infection target.
Study the linked scenario lesson for reassessment, source-control and population-specific boundaries.

scope_limits: The tutor teaches AUC targets and monitoring decisions, not an unvalidated patient-specific Bayesian calculator or a universal culture-directed osteomyelitis prescription.

scenarioLedger.title: Sepsis-3 Definition, Diagnosis, and 1-Hour Bundle
facts: For possible/probable/definite septic shock or probable/definite sepsis without shock, give antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour. Possible sepsis without shock requires rapid investigation and reassessment of infectious likelihood.
Obtain cultures promptly when they will not substantially delay therapy; select by suspected source, prior isolates, recent antibiotics, severity and local resistance.
Urgently assess required source control; SSC 2026 suggests early control, ideally within 6 hours when required.
Use MRSA/MDR and anaerobic coverage according to risk/source; do not add every spectrum class to every case. Reassess and narrow when evidence permits.

scenarioLedger.title: Cirrhosis Complications — Varices, SBP, Hepatic Encephalopathy, and HCC Surveillance
facts: Ascitic PMN >=250 cells/mm3 can support SBP despite negative culture; do not require positive culture. Cirrhotic GI bleeding is a conditional prophylaxis indication.
SBP adjunct albumin eligibility: serum creatinine >1 mg/dL, BUN >30 mg/dL or bilirubin >4 mg/dL; IV albumin 1.5 g/kg initially and 1 g/kg day 3. Assess volume status and local protocol.

Primary prophylaxis consideration requires ascitic protein <1.5 g/dL plus renal dysfunction (Cr >=1.2 mg/dL, BUN >=25 mg/dL or Na <=130 mEq/L) OR liver failure (Child-Pugh >=9 AND bilirubin >=3 mg/dL).
Study the linked scenario lesson for reassessment, source-control and population-specific boundaries.

decisionLessons.title: COPD — severe exacerbation and antibiotic reassessment
facts: Assess pneumonia, sepsis and respiratory failure; antibiotics do not replace bronchodilator, steroid and ventilatory decisions.

Use severity, sputum change, prior cultures/antibiotic exposure and local resistance to select oral versus IV therapy. Ventilated/severely ill patients need inpatient management and culture-directed review.
Review IV therapy promptly for narrowing/oral conversion as the patient improves; reassess lack of improvement and obtain cultures rather than repeatedly extending an empiric oral course.
gaps: Resistant-pathogen therapy requires the current isolate/local antibiogram; no single universal ventilator-associated regimen applies to every COPD exacerbation.

decisionLessons.title: UTI — obstruction, catheter, resistant organisms and prostatitis

decisionLessons.title: STIs — recurrence, pregnancy, allergy and congenital infection
facts: Verify diagnosis, adherence and reexposure before resistance. Persistent trichomonas without reexposure needs susceptibility/specialist assessment; complicated compounded vaginal salvage is not an interchangeable commercial oral product.
CDC resistant-trichomonas options after high-dose failure require specialist coordination; IgE nitroimidazole allergy calls for supervised desensitization. Tinidazole should be avoided in pregnancy.
For selected recurrent symptomatic BV, ACOG 2025 supports concurrent partner treatment; do not repeat the older CDC 2021 statement against routine partner treatment as a universal current rule.
Pregnancy syphilis has no proven nonpenicillin substitute: specialist-supervised desensitization followed by stage-appropriate penicillin. Late-latent intervals >9 days require restarting the course.

For congenital syphilis, maternal treatment, neonatal examination/titer and completeness of evaluation determine single-dose eligibility versus ten days; follow reactive neonatal titers every 2-3 months until negative.

After resistant trichomonas high-dose failure, CDC describes specialist-directed oral plus compounded intravaginal tinidazole for 14 days, and another paromomycin-containing salvage option. Product/compounding and susceptibility review are mandatory; do not use an ordinary BV gel as a substitute.
gaps: Resistance and desensitization are supervised protocols; pregnancy and congenital cases cannot use the nonpregnant adult alternatives by default.

decisionLessons.title: Skin infection — diabetic foot, osteomyelitis and IV monitoring
facts: Assess infection severity, bone involvement and perfusion; uninfected ulcers do not need antibiotics. Obtain appropriate deep-tissue/bone specimens when indicated rather than using colonizing surface flora alone.

Severe infection, deep abscess, necrosis or ischemia needs urgent surgical/vascular assessment. Select therapy by severity, culture, recent antibiotics and local resistance; no routine empiric Pseudomonas coverage for every temperate-climate mild DFI.
Soft tissue usually 1-2 weeks; positive bone margin after minor amputation up to 3 weeks; unresected osteomyelitis 6 weeks. Reevaluate nonresponse rather than automatically prolonging.

Invasive MRSA vancomycin uses AUC24 400-600 mg*h/L, assuming MIC 1 mg/L; use measured concentrations, changing renal function and validated pharmacy support. Dialysis modality changes the sampling and redosing plan.

Selected mild Gram-positive DFI and culture-defined MSSA unresected osteomyelitis have separate loaded courses. For other cultured pathogens use an active regimen and source-control plan; a dose is not selected from the culture result alone without site, renal function and allergy review.
gaps: The tutor teaches AUC targets and monitoring decisions, not an unvalidated patient-specific Bayesian calculator or a universal culture-directed osteomyelitis prescription.

decisionLessons.title: H pylori — failed therapy and susceptibility-guided rescue

decisionLessons.title: Pertussis — exact age boundaries, pregnancy and resistance
facts: CDC Table 4 places exactly 6 months in the >=6-month azithromycin schedule; <6 months uses 10 mg/kg/day for all 5 days. Avoid silent gaps between age bands.

Current CDC guidance permits TMP-SMX alternatives at >=2 months when appropriate; pregnancy is excluded from the older CDC TMP-SMX pertussis recommendation. Macrolide-allergic pregnancy requires specialist selection rather than automatic TMP-SMX substitution.
Infant macrolide use has pyloric-stenosis risk, yet CDC still favors azithromycin in very young infants because pertussis can be life-threatening. Monitor and counsel.

Consider geography/exposure and current resistance guidance; consult public health/ID for suspected resistant infection and selected PEP contacts. Routine acute bronchitis remains an antibiotic-avoidance diagnosis.
gaps: Macrolide-allergic pregnancy and rare resistance require supervised selection; ordinary bronchitis is not a substitute indication.
Independent clinical review pending; educational decisions do not constitute an individualized prescription.

facts: Uncomplicated diffuse otitis externa generally starts with topical therapy. Verify administration and whether obstruction needs clinician-performed aural toilet/wick placement.

facts: Obtain appropriate blood cultures/echo and involve the endocarditis team. Organism, susceptibility, valve/device status and embolic/heart-failure complications determine antibiotics and surgery.
MSSA native-valve, E faecalis dual-beta-lactam and HACEK courses are separate loaded lessons. Prosthetic staphylococcal infection has a different combination/duration and toxicity burden.
MRSA IV vancomycin requires AUC/renal monitoring; susceptibility and response may require an alternative specialist regimen.
Culture-negative disease requires review of prior antibiotics, epidemiology and fastidious organisms; a negative routine culture is not proof that empirical therapy should be identical in every case.

decisionLessons.title: Rheumatic fever — eradication versus secondary prophylaxis
facts: Secondary prevention is distinct from the acute eradication course; adherence support and access to repeated prophylaxis are central.
ACC/AHA adult secondary prevention includes benzathine penicillin G 1.2 million units IM every 4 weeks. Document the last RF episode, carditis and persistent valve disease.

Persistent valvular disease generally requires at least 10 years or until age 40, whichever is longer; higher-risk patients may need longer. Without residual disease, duration differs and requires confirmation of the applicable age/carditis branch.
Confirmed allergy requires a separate preventive option; assess phenotype rather than confusing daily oral prevention with an acute ten-day GAS regimen.
gaps: Child weight cutoffs and shortened injection intervals vary across protocols; use the named population-specific protocol rather than merging thresholds.
Independent clinical review pending; educational decisions do not constitute an individualized prescription.

medication_safety.population: Adults; stated formulation and indication only.
contraindications: Prior hypersensitivity to clindamycin or lincomycin.

hepatic.guidance: Half-life can increase in moderate/severe liver disease; adjustment may not be necessary, but monitor liver enzymes in severe disease. No Child-Pugh reduction formula.

renal.guidance: Isolated renal impairment generally needs no adjustment at usual adult doses up to 2 g/day. Combined significant renal and hepatic dysfunction requires caution and a maximum of 2 g/day.

hepatic.guidance: Isolated hepatic dysfunction generally needs no adjustment; combined significant renal dysfunction limits dosing to 2 g/day.

interactions: Do not mix or simultaneously infuse with calcium-containing IV solutions. Neonatal restrictions differ.
monitoring: Monitor prothrombin time with low vitamin K stores or impaired synthesis, including chronic hepatic disease.
gaps: The 2 g/day ceiling is not the gonorrhea prescription or a universal maximum for all indications. Do not use older label STI dosing instead of CDC guidance.
